messages:
Ivy: quick note — demo produced a short burst of 503s when the gateway blocked on admission. We need a nonblocking boundary ASAP.
Theo: can you paste the tiny trace? curious if it was token checkout or lease reconcile.
Ivy: tail:
```
2026-06-07T09:14:22Z ingress-gw WARN req=zz1 wait=910ms hold=admission
2026-06-07T09:14:22Z admission-svc ERR req=zz1 reconcile=slow
2026-06-07T09:14:22Z ingress-gw ERR req=zz1 respond=503
```
Ivy: gateway sat waiting and then cascaded failures. Two high-level patterns: fast-fail at gw vs provisional permits.
Rina: fast-fail is simple and keeps p99 tight but hurts client UX. provisional permits reduce visible failures but add accounting and abuse surface.
Omar: sketch a tiny proto: AdmitResult { enum Type { ALLOW=0; TEMP_ALLOW=1; DENY=2 } Type type; string grant_id; int32 temp_ttl_ms; string fallback; }
Claire: If TEMP_ALLOW is used, gw must tag traffic and place it in a low-priority work queue so confirmed grants can preempt it. Also capture provisional=true metrics.
Theo: reconciliation model: admission eventually emits Confirm(grant_id) or Revoke(grant_id). On Revoke we increment provisional_revoke, run refund logic, and mark tenant for tighter provisional quotas.
Rina: Billing policy debate: charge-on-issue + reconcile refunds vs delayed charge until confirm. I prefer charge-on-issue to avoid unpaid bursts and simplify billing, with auditable refunds on revoke.
Ivy: agree. charging immediately reduces abuse incentive; refunds must be traceable and rate-limited.
Omar: add an in-gateway memo cache keyed by tenant+route TTL=600ms to reduce stampede to admission for hot keys. Also bound per-tenant provisional rate (eg provisional_qps_limit).
Claire: telemetry we need up-front: temp_issued, temp_revoked, temp_ttl_hist, reconcile_refunds_total, provisional_latency_{p50,p95,p99} per-route, and a provisional_revoked_rate alert. Tag by tenant+priority_class.
Theo: experiment plan: gate TEMP_ALLOW to low-cost routes (embeds, short completion) only. Staging smoke -> 1% prod -> 5% prod over 72h if metrics look good. Add synthetic burst sim to validate fairness.
Rina: implementation owners: Ivy -> RFC + proto, Omar -> gateway changes + cache, Claire -> billing/refund pipeline, Theo -> telemetry + canary dashboard. I'll prototype a small simulator for bursty clients to sanity-check fairness heuristics.
Ivy: thanks. I'll open the RFC this afternoon and link the simulation and telemetry PRs. small decision: provisional requests should be charged at full rate on issue and reconciled with refunds if revoked. thumbs-up?
All: +1
Ivy: will follow up with a minimal spike test and a runbook for provisional revocations.
